title: Keyframe Editor (Box Animation)
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a keyframe animation editor for a box on a 0–5 second timeline: support adding keyframes, play/pause, time scrubbing, and switching between linear/smooth interpolation.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Functionality]
(1) Use one BoxGeometry as the object being edited; choose its initial position freely.
(2) The timeline range is [0, 5] seconds; internally store a keyframe list of {t, x, y, z} (or quaternions; if only position is animated, the first three components are sufficient).
(3) id="addKeyframeBtn": At the current currentTime, write the box's current position to a keyframe (if a keyframe already exists at the same t, overwrite it; explain this behavior in a comment).
(4) id="playPauseBtn": Toggle playback/pause; during playback, currentTime must either loop or be clamped within 0–5s.
(5) id="timeSlider": <input type="range" min="0" max="5" step="0.01" />. Whether scrubbing pauses playback or allows it to continue must be documented by the implementation, but __3D_STATE__.currentTime must match the slider.
(6) id="interpSelect": A <select> with option values "linear" and "smooth" (smooth may be implemented using Catmull-Rom, a spline, smoothstep, or a similar method).

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  keyframeCount: number,
  currentTime: number,       // Seconds, 0..5
  isPlaying: boolean,
  interpType: string,        // "linear" | "smooth"
  objectPos: { x, y, z }     // Box world position, consistent with the interpolation result
}

Output a single HTML file that runs when opened directly in a browser.
